title: Lorenzo Tio and Papa Tio as clarinet teachers
summary: Few Black music teachers existed; Bigard's own teacher was Lorenzo Tio, whose uncle Papa Tio bluntly turned away pupils without talent and took a liking to Bigard.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Well, weren't there any colored music teachers or --

Only a few. That's what I said. Trumpet players, like Manuel Perez was a trumpet player, and they had some -- another good trumpet player, he was real light and he would pass for white and he wouldn't teach no colored at all.

Now, my teacher was Mexican. Tio, Lorenzo Tio. And his whole family was clarinet players from the great grandfather on down, the whole family. And his uncle -- we used to call him Papa Tio -- he was a better musician than his nephew, Lorenzo Tio. And he wouldn't take any -- he was a very peculiar man. If he'd take a pupil -- and the first lesson he'd give him and he could see that he wasn't going to be any good playing the clarinet, he'd tell him, "Son, I don't want your money." He said, "You want to be a clarinet player." He says, "Try something else." He said, "You don't have it." He'd tell them right off the bat. And nine times out of ten he was right.
